newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says Labour windfall tax would damage UK.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says Labour windfall tax would damage UK.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said the opposition Labour party's plans to impose a windfall tax on privatised utilities such as British Telecom would hurt Britain's economic performance.
Labour has not specified which companies will be hit by the tax but Clarke said he assumed BT would be included.
He told a news conference that the improved telecoms services delivered by BT had been an important factor in attracting foreign investment to Britain.
"British Telecoms is one of the most successful privatisations we've had," Clarke said.
"To bang them with a tax and to load the costs of a tax on British Telecoms is contrary to the interests of UK Ltd. It would damage our excellent economic performance."
"The windfall tax, which as I understand it is due to raise either three billion pounds or five billion pounds out of key British industries, is a serious threat to our continued recovery."
Labour's finance spokesman Gordon Brown said earlier that the windfall tax, intended to finance job-creation programmes for young people, would be a one-off levy.

"It will be levied fairly. There will be consultation with the regulators and it is restricted only to these privatised utilities that were sold off at an under-valuation and have had lax regulatory regimes."

Clarke attacked Labour's windfall tax plans as a "dreadfully old-fashioned method of claiming to create jobs" and said it was disgraceful that Labour had still not specified how much revenue the windfall tax would raise or which companies would be affected.
